title: Fuel Metering Unit Delivery Nozzle — Removal
abstract: Removal of a fuel metering unit delivery nozzle with the engine on wing, including draining of the unit, immediate capping of the fuel connections and the shroud handling that protects the clearance to the cowl latch.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove one delivery nozzle from the fuel metering unit with the engine installed, for replacement or for bench examination.
sections.job_setup_note: Fuel work on the engine needs the aircraft grounded, the area clear of ignition sources and a drain rig with the correct capacity. Get the capping plug set before you open any connection: an open fuel line in the nacelle collects debris in seconds and a contaminated nozzle will not pass its bench check. Two people are needed, one at the drain rig.
sections.procedure: 1. Make the aircraft safe for fuel system work and put the warning notices in position. 2. WARNING: DO NOT WORK ON THE FUEL SYSTEM WITH AN IGNITION SOURCE IN THE AREA. FUEL VAPOUR COLLECTS IN THE LOWER COWL. 3. Open the fan cowl and support it on the stay. 4. Connect the drain rig and drain the metering unit to the collection container. 5. Disconnect the electrical connection at the unit and tag it. 6. Loosen the nozzle union nut and break the joint. 7. CAUTION: CAP EVERY OPEN FUEL CONNECTION IMMEDIATELY. AN UNCAPPED LINE IN THE NACELLE WILL PICK UP DEBRIS. 8. Remove the nozzle from the unit and cap the port. 9. Examine the nozzle shroud for witness marking against the cowl latch and record what you find. 10. Put the nozzle in its transport container with the removal record. 11. Measure and record the clearance between the cowl latch and the shroud at the closed position before the cowl is left open.
sections.close_out: Leave the capping plugs in position and the drain rig connected if the installation does not follow immediately. Record the removal, the nozzle part number and serial number, the witness marking and the measured latch clearance in the aircraft technical log.

safety_precautions: Make the aircraft safe for fuel system work and remove ignition sources from the area.
Cap every open fuel connection immediately.
